name: WAS lab run parameters
description: The environment, the channel, and any WAS object name the site wants to set rather than derive. A name left blank is composed by roles/model/vars/naming.yml; a name filled in wins.

spec.question_description: The environment this build is for. It is an answer, not a property of a machine: the same host can be built as any environment. Two to eight characters, starting with a letter, letters and digits only - it becomes part of a cell name, a profile name and a filesystem path. No list of allowed codes is enforced; any code the site uses is accepted.

The network channel, which becomes the first part of the cell name and the last three letters of the cluster name. Title case is the canonical form, because that is how it appears inside WAS object names.

What gets built. standalone is one application server profile carrying its own administrative console - no deployment manager, no node agent, no cluster. nd is a deployment manager profile plus one federated node per machine in the node agent group, which is what a cluster needs. It is asked rather than derived because a single host can legitimately be either. The installed binaries are identical; only the manageprofiles template differs.
Leave blank to derive it as <Channel>_<ENVIRONMENT>. Fill it in to impose a name the pattern would not produce.
Leave blank to derive it as Cluster<first three letters of the channel, upper case>. Fill it in for a cluster that does not follow that rule.

How many application server JVMs each federated node carries - this is the VERTICAL axis of the cluster. The horizontal axis is not asked: it is how many hosts the node agent group holds, one member on each. Two here over two nodes is four JVMs. Members beyond the first on a node are given their own ports by WAS (genUniquePorts), because two JVMs on one node cannot share WC_defaulthost, SOAP and ORB; pin them with was_cluster_member_ports in the inventory when a predictable port is needed. The upper bound is 8, and it is a guard against a number typed into the wrong field: every member is a full JVM with its own heap.

The cluster member, which is one JVM. Leave blank to derive it as <cluster>_<node>_<index>. A value here names the member on every host in the run, so a per-host name belongs in the inventory instead. It names ONE member: filling this in and answering more than one server per node is refused, because appending an index to a name you chose by hand would invent a convention you did not ask for - declare was_cluster_member_names as a list in the inventory for that.

The WAS node: the deployment manager node on a dmgr host, the node agent node elsewhere. Leave blank to derive it. A value here applies to every host in the run - declare was_node_name per host in the inventory when the machines differ.
Leave blank to derive it as Dmgr_<ENVIRONMENT>_<Channel>. One host can hold two cells during a migration, which is why this name carries both.

spec.question_name: I confirm this run may touch PRODUCTION
spec.question_description: Must be answered true to run against an environment whose tier is prod. Defaulted to false on purpose: reaching production should never be the result of picking the wrong answer. The workflow carries an Approval Node for the same reason at the other end.
